selection.scope: Ten deliberately selected public, open OpenEuroLLM/Taskboard issues spanning training throughput, evaluation quality, explicit dependencies, memory failures and automation
selection.sampling: Purposeful case study selected before measuring graph impact coverage. Not random, exhaustive, or a ranking of all OpenEuroLLM work.
selection.question: Which changes could plausibly remove a documented bottleneck or speed up work, and what evidence would be required to establish an actual improvement?
selection.claim_policy: An issue title, a GitHub link, an author-reported result and a controlled speedup are different levels of evidence. The report verifies literal source phrases but does not validate experimental measurements or claim causal impact. Comments are source-hashed for the ten selected issues only.

cases.candidate: Validate the revised sequence-to-worker assignment before production adoption.
cases.next_check: Reproduce throughput and complete the pending memory, save and resume acceptance checks.

evidence.meaning: A revised assignment was timed above the earlier 94–99k-token/s production range.
Issue authors report a controlled comparison, not independently reproduced here.
Production validation is explicitly outstanding.

cases.next_check: Compare configurations on the same hardware and power envelope; do not treat reference H100 numbers as a demonstrated speedup.

evidence.needle: Scaling EP instead of PP or TP seems to be the way to go

cases.candidate: Isolate the chat-template/thinking-adherence effect with a same-base control.
